instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: We are mapping the brake fluid flush and bleed procedure for your e-bike and bicycles. The job ensures zero leaks, correct fluid type per the lever stamp, and a rock-solid lever feel that doesn't pull to the bar within two attempts.

draft.title: Brake Fluid Flush and Bleed
disqualifiers: Any fluid wetness or weeping at hoses or fittings after bleeding.
Brake lever remains spongy or pulls to the handlebar after two bleed attempts.
releases: Safe to ride in city traffic and on gravel.

steps.title: Identify and Verify Brake Fluid Type
steps.explanation: Using the wrong fluid swells the seals and ruins the brakes within a week.

fields.prompt: Enter the fluid type stamped on the lever body or reservoir cap.
fields.acceptance_target: stamp on the lever body or reservoir cap
fields.guidance: Only use the exact fluid type stamped on the brake hardware (e.g., Mineral Oil or DOT).

steps.title: Flush and Bleed Brake System
steps.explanation: Flushing the old fluid and air out ensures full hydraulic pressure and prevents brake failure.

fields.prompt: Did you follow the manufacturer's service guide for this specific brake system?
fields.guidance: Refer to the manufacturer's service guide for the correct step-by-step bleed sequence.

steps.title: Verify Lever Feel
steps.explanation: The lever must feel rock solid to ensure there is no air left in the system.

fields.prompt: Pull the brake lever hard. Does it feel rock solid and stop short of the handlebar?
choices: Yes, rock solid and does not pull back to the bar
No, spongy or pulls back to the bar
fields.acceptance_target: Yes, rock solid and does not pull back to the bar
fields.guidance: The lever must feel completely solid and must not contact the handlebar grip under pressure.

fields.prompt: How many bleed attempts were required to get a solid feel?
fields.guidance: If the lever is still spongy after two tries, stop and get someone else to look at it.

steps.title: Inspect for Leaks
steps.explanation: Any slow leak will lead to sudden brake failure while riding.

fields.prompt: Are all hoses, fittings, and connections completely dry with no fluid weeping?
fields.guidance: The bike must not leave the stand if there is any wetness at all on the hoses or fittings.
